Compared the entire source def:visible, the preceding geometric crossing/Gauss definitions, and the labelled-tuple/cyclic-representative conventions in def:polygon and its formalization remark with SM.visible_signature_definition and the concrete definitions and proofs giving its type meaning. The aggregate assumes only the inherited n>=3, the actual real planar labelled tuple P, and Generic P. visibleSignature is exactly the turn tuple, actual finite set of unordered geometrically crossing edge pairs, and the independently constructed geometric Gauss word embedded into a common support alphabet. Turns are the source chirotope turns with the previously reviewed determinant convention. The second projection has membership precisely IsCrossing P s, so it contains every actual remote-edge crossing and no artificial crossing predicate. The third projection is explicitly the previously verified gaussWord mapped by Crossing P's Subtype.val. This injective letter map forgets only proof-carrying subtype data: cycle_map_injective proves that it is injective on entire cyclic words, preserving all repeated letters and distinguishing every source rotation class. Cycle remains the inspected genuine list-rotation quotient, without reversal or arbitrary-permutation identification. The aggregate also proves that its word letters are exactly its crossing set and that its length is twice the actual crossing cardinality. The inherited Gauss construction gives exactly two occurrences of each actual crossing and sorts actual interior visits on the half-open traversal circle; no arbitrary input word, crossing naming, root or order witness is supplied.

Constancy is proved geometrically, not encoded as a definition or an extra hypothesis. crossingTransport is the canonical equivalence between actual crossing subtypes when their predicates agree, and visitTransport preserves the underlying unordered support and visited edge label exactly. The predicate equality is derived from chirotope constancy in continuous preconnected generic families. crossing_support_partner extracts the other edge from the actual two-element support, and crossingParameter_eq_of_support_pair identifies its actual intersection parameter with the previously reviewed Cramer formula. Same-edge visit comparisons therefore use the proved continuous generic crossing-order theorem. That theorem explicitly handles equal partner labels, for which both strict comparisons are false, and handles distinct partners by Generic's exclusion of coincident crossing points. Visits on different edges are compared by their unchanged edge-block labels in the traversal order. Thus generic_family_visitKey_lt and generic_family_visitKey_le cover all visit pairs, without an omitted equality case or a hidden distinct-partner premise. The target Gauss list is independently constructed: its equality with the canonically transported source list follows from bijective inventory, no duplicate visits, and sorted-list uniqueness under the actual target geometric key. Projection then proves actual cycle and word transport. Mapping crossing supports gives exact equality of support words, and the turn and crossing-set proofs give equality of the full triple.

visibleSignature_labelledChamber applies this family theorem to the subtype of the actual connected component in the genuine generic locus, using its canonical continuous inclusion and its preconnectedness. It does not replace a chamber by a signature class or assume a path, word equality, or desired wall law. Relabelling is proved for all three independently constructed projections. Under shift a P at new label i=P(i+a), the new turn at i reads the old turn at i+a, whereas each old edge index in a crossing support and in a word letter moves to i-a. visibleSignatureShift implements exactly these actions; its identity and composition laws are proved. crossingSet_shift uses the genuine crossingShiftEquiv, and gaussSupportWord_shift uses the previously reviewed gaussWord_shift theorem comparing independently sorted words through a cut rotation. Consequently the numerical cut does not introduce a distinguished vertex, a reversal, or an arbitrary label permutation.

The quotient-chamber clause quantifies over every generic representative Q whose actual cyclic quotient projection belongs to the chamber of P. The accepted geometric preimage decomposition places Q in the labelled connected component of an actual shift of P. Labelled constancy and the proved shift law then give an actual a in ZMod n with signature(Q)=visibleSignatureShift(a,signature(P)). This is the source's full explicitly permitted labelled/equivariant reading: def:polygon states representative invariance up to induced index relabelling, and the formalization remark permits labelled tuples throughout with recorded shift-equivariance. A separately constructed quotient of signature data is therefore not required, and equality of raw labelled triples across arbitrary representatives is not being substituted for the source convention. Empty crossing sets are admitted throughout: there is no nonempty-word or chosen-crossing hypothesis, the finite sort and maps produce the empty cyclic word, and all inventory, length, transport and constancy arguments cover that case.

The source, all 32 inspected local supporting files, and the recomputed semantic dependency hash match the passed checkpoint-017 development receipt. The eight new files are unchanged from this independent full review, and the 24 inherited files are byte-identical to earlier independent reviews. The receipt audits 588 project declarations and 16 mapped claims with only the standard propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound axioms and explicitly leaves stage_accepted false. This review certifies only the complete original DEFINE row def:visible. It does not assert that signatures classify chambers, does not certify constancy on weak visible chambers, and does not certify the corner state sum or its main wall-crossing and soft-theorem targets. Supporting transport and sorting helpers are not counted as additional original claims.

countersignature_20260913.reason: Source (sm-1-polygons.tex:270-276): the visible signature of a generic P is the triple ((tau_i)_{i in Z/n}, X(P), Gauss word of P), constant on chambers by prop:chambers. Lean `visibleSignature hn P hP : (ZMod n -> SignType) x Finset (Finset (ZMod n)) x Cycle (Finset (ZMod n))` unfolds to `(turn P, crossingSet P, gaussSupportWord hn hP)` (VisibleSignature.lean:12-13,43-46) under exactly the source hypotheses n>=3 and `Generic P = G1 P /\ G2 P` (Generic.lean:11-19, matching def:generic (G1),(G2) with edgeInterior = relative interior). Component 1: `turn P i = chi P (i-1) i (i+1)`, `chi = sign det(P j - P i, P k - P i)` (Chirotope.lean:10-14) is def:chirotope verbatim (tex:63-67). Component 2: `crossingSet P` has membership `IsCrossing P s := exists i j, s={i,j} /\ remote i j /\ (edgeSegment P i ∩ edgeSegment P j).Nonempty` (Crossings.lean:12-19), with remote/adjacent as in def:polygon (Polygon.lean:63-66; tex:44-46) — exactly X(P) of def:crossings (tex:130-133). Component 3: `gaussWord = (gaussCycle).map Sigma.fst`, `gaussCycle = (gaussList : Cycle (Visit P))`, `gaussList = Finset.univ.sort` under the order lifted from `visitKey v = (edge index).val + crossingParameter` (GaussWord.lean:17-24,84-89; GaussVisits.lean:17,45-50,85-86; Traversal.lean:12-17). `Visit P = Σ c : Crossing P, {i // i ∈ c.val}` gives exactly the two visits (i,t_ij),(j,t_ji) per crossing; the ascending sort (gaussList_sorted) realises the traversal order of Gamma(P) cut at label 0, and Mathlib's `Cycle` (list-rotation quotient) forgets the cut, so this is def:gauss (tex:245-254): the cyclic sequence of the 2|X(P)| visits, each labelled by its crossing. Mapping each `Crossing P` letter to its underlying 2-element Finset (`gaussSupportWord`) is an injective re-encoding of the alphabet (clause 4 of the theorem proves injectivity on whole cyclic words), so no information is lost. The second sentence of the definition is captured twice: clause 7 (constancy on `labelledChamber = connectedComponent` in `GenericTuple n`, i.e. components of U_n under the product topology on ZMod n -> R x R) and clause 9 (for `chamber = connectedComponent` in `GenericPolygon n = Quotient (cyclicSetoid comap val)`, i.e. U_n/(Z/n) with quotient topology, equality up to `visibleSignatureShift a`). The 'exists a' reading is the correct one for the quotient: def:polygon (tex:32-36) and its formalization remark (tex:52-58) state every notion is introduced on a representative and is invariant under sigma only up to the induced relabelling of indices, and literal equality of labelled triples across representatives is false in general. `visibleSignatureShift a (t,X,w) = (i ↦ t(i+a), X.image (translateSupport (-a)), w.map (translateSupport (-a)))` (VisibleRelabel.lean:19-22; CrossingEquiv.lean:9-10) is the induced relabelling for `shift a P = fun i => P (i+a)` (Polygon.lean:22-23): new turn i = old turn i+a, old crossing {i,j} -> {i-a,j-a}. Nothing is vacuous: hypotheses are satisfiable (any triangle in general position), no sorry/axiom in the 32-module import closure. sm15_reworded is false and CHANGES_SINCE_20260909.md does not mention def:visible; the SM15 excerpt is byte-identical to SM12's. The existing review (reviews/def-visible.json) reaches the same verdict on the same grounds; I read it only after forming this judgement.

Clauses 5-6 (VisibleDefinition.lean:17-19): letters of the word are exactly the crossings and length = 2 * |X(P)|; the source states these only implicitly in def:gauss ('2|X(P)| visits, each labelled by its crossing').

Clause 8 (VisibleDefinition.lean:22-24): explicit shift-equivariance visibleSignature (shift a P) = visibleSignatureShift a (visibleSignature P); the source asserts this only as the blanket convention of def:polygon (tex:36-38).
Clauses 10-11 (VisibleDefinition.lean:29-31): action laws visibleSignatureShift 0 = id and composition; pure bookkeeping, not in the source.

The underlying definitions turn, IsCrossing, crossingSet are total on all labelled tuples (no (G1) precondition), whereas the source defines X(P) only under (G1) (tex:130); visibleSignature itself is only formed under Generic P, so this does not affect the row.
